clue.text: Fat hares consorting with these insects?

parts.note: butter is a cooking fat
to hare is to rush along, so hares means flies

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about which insects keep company with plump hares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat hares' reads as plump animals, but it is two words of wordplay: a noun for a fat and a verb meaning races.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterflies are a large order of winged insects with scaly, often brightly coloured wings.

clue.text: Forearmed with them?

parts.note: playfully reads forearmed as having the long bones that run through the lower arm

explanation.definitionFit: The two long bones of the human forearm are the radius and this pair's namesake bone on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Short-tempered if going in to take the stand

indicators.note: the word if is said to be going into the synonym for short-tempered

parts.note: testy means irritable or short-tempered
taken as written

explanation.surface: An irritable witness has to be coaxed into the witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the stand is to give evidence as a witness in court, which is to give sworn testimony.

clue.text: Save and buy back

definitions.meaning: to save a soul or a situation, rescue it
to recover a pawned item by paying for it

explanation.surface: A short description of good financial practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Redemption covers both rescuing a sinner and reclaiming a pledged article for money.

clue.text: Pines at head of river well rooted, with this intent?

indicators.note: the synonym for pines is placed at the front of the river's name

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it, so pines means longs
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: Pine trees growing firmly at the source of a river, with a camper wondering about staying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with this intent?' puns on 'in tent': a camper settling in for a lengthy visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-stay visitor is settled for a lengthy period, hence well rooted, as on a long camping holiday.

clue.text: Avenger is out to make an impression

indicators.note: being out suggests the letters of avenger are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An avenger is on the loose, trying to make his mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving cuts a design into metal or stone, literally making an impression in the surface.

clue.text: Dizzy — lacking energy second time mother's under the weather

indicators.note: dizzy suggests the letters are spinning and come out in a new order
lacking tells us to take away the letter standing for energy from the pool

parts.note: mother plus the s of the possessive
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Feeling giddy and drained, a second time mother is under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dizzy' scrambles S, T and MOTHERSUNDER once 'lacking' has removed one E (energy). 'under the weather' looks like an idiom for ill, but 'under' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Storms with lightning and rumbles from the sky are a kind of weather condition.

clue.text: Female clothing covering legs, primarily — topping for the house

indicators.note: the underwear word is said to cover, so it goes round the other letter

parts.note: panties are women's underwear

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word legs

explanation.surface: Women's underwear covering the legs, oddly linked to the top of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved roof tiles called pantiles cover the top of many buildings.

clue.text: Rich man signed off from retailing project

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are spoiled or out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy man has signed off from a shop-based venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signed off' looks like a phrase meaning quit, but 'off' is the anagram signal and 'signed' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchandising is the promotion and sale of goods in shops, a commercial venture in selling.

clue.text: Queues, we hear, to give tips

definitions.meaning: queues sounds like cues, which are prompts or suggestions
tips are pieces of useful advice

explanation.surface: People standing in lines are told how to give gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense works through sound: queues is said like 'cues', and cues are prompts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cues and tips are both small suggestions or prompts that guide someone.

clue.text: Blacken, camouflaging a red tinge

indicators.note: camouflaging disguises the letters of a red tinge by mixing them up

explanation.surface: Painting something black to hide a reddish tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blacken' looks literal, but here means to blacken someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken a reputation is to defame or belittle someone unfairly.

clue.text: Pollution the result when can is dropped into loch

indicators.note: the two words are dropped into the name of the Scottish loch

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Dumping a tin can in a Scottish lake results in pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness here is foulness or filth, a sense close to contamination.

clue.text: Worker in charge of the frolic

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee in charge of the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful caper or prank, a piece of foolery.

clue.text: Reform by Rome-a new development

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so the letters of by Rome are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reform imposed by Rome, a fresh political start.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is something at its earliest stage of growth, a fresh beginning.

clue.text: Holiday home great — but falling apart

parts.note: a short holiday is a break
at home means in
G is short for great, as in G-string pun

explanation.surface: A great holiday home that is crumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something breaking is coming to pieces, disintegrating.

clue.text: Arrived, returning a sickly shrub

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: returning tells us to read a and the word for sickly backwards

parts.note: ill means sickly

explanation.surface: A sick plant came back after arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is an evergreen flowering bush related to the tea plant.

clue.text: Ships from port and starboard engulfed in raging waters?

indicators.note: the side letters are swallowed up in stormy waters, so all these letters are churned together into a new order

parts.note: L for left, the port side
R for right, the starboard side

explanation.surface: Ships lost from both sides in a storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfed in raging' throws L (port) and R (starboard) into WATERS and churns the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Trawlers are fishing boats that drag nets along the sea.

clue.text: Transport taking guides around before noon

indicators.note: the word for guides goes around the abbreviation for the morning

parts.note: steers means guides
AM, ante meridiem, is before noon

explanation.surface: Tour guides take a morning ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamers are steam-powered ships, a form of travel by water.

clue.text: Sea denizen manta's put in a tizzy with ease, it's said

indicators.note: being put in a tizzy means flustered, so one letter of manta is shifted to a new spot

parts.note: manta, with the 's read as is

indicators.note: it's said marks a word judged by its sound

parts.note: ease sounds like 'E's', two letter Es

explanation.surface: A manta ray gets flustered easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in a tizzy' shifts the T of MANTA to make MANAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee, or sea cow, is a large aquatic mammal of warm coastal waters.

clue.text: Uranium covered by shifting dunes hadn't been exploited

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective describing something untouched

indicators.note: uranium is covered by the dunes, placed inside them
shifting sands move, so the letters of dunes rearrange

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Uranium buried under drifting sand had never been mined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused has not yet been put to work or drawn upon.

clue.text: Translation of Butler's "Erewhon"? It can't be found!

indicators.note: translation here means rendering the letters of the title in a new order

explanation.surface: A joke about rendering Samuel Butler's novel title into plain English.
explanation.walkthrough: Erewhon is the 1872 satire by Samuel Butler; 'Translation of' rearranges its title, the possessive merely naming the author.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that cannot be located is literally in no place at all.

clue.text: Quails seeing off English crows

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Quail birds see off some English crows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quails' looks like a plural noun for birds, beside 'crows', but it is a verb meaning shrinks in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, as one does when cringing.

clue.text: Duck with a range of knowledge of one wood

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
ken is one's range of knowledge

explanation.surface: A duck with considerable knowledge of a particular forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken describes things made of oak timber, one type of wood.

clue.text: Was parking among trees — attracting horntails!

indicators.note: among says the pieces are placed within the word for trees

parts.note: woods are areas of trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone parked among trees and attracted stinging insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Horntails are sawfly-like insects whose larvae bore into timber, also called by this name.

clue.text: Sail at sea — cold, and it's salty

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of sail are mixed up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Sailing on a cold sea, with salty spray.
explanation.definitionFit: The word relates to salt-like mineral content, a technical adjective for a briny quality.

clue.text: For this creature, larger amounts offered to me not accepted

indicators.note: the larger-amount word accepts not, taking it inside

parts.note: more means greater quantities
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bigger offers were made to me, but turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: A monotreme is an egg-laying mammal such as the platypus or echidna.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotreme is an egg-laying mammal, an unusual kind of animal.

clue.text: Two different measurements provided for her

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
an en is a printer's unit of width

explanation.surface: Two distinct measurements were taken for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's name, so 'her' stands for a female person.

clue.text: Resolution, with small change, fussy sister incorporated

indicators.note: the scrambled sister is incorporated within the coins

parts.note: pence are small coins

indicators.note: fussy suggests fiddly rearrangement of the letters of sister

explanation.surface: A resolution with small amendments, a fussy sister included.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution here means determination, steadfastness in keeping going.
